notes: Curated swap rules. A rule says: in a dish where one of the 'from' foods is a main ingredient, replace a fraction of it (by mass) with the 'to' food. Rules are food-agnostic: nothing here assumes beef.

replaceFraction is NOT authored. The generator computes it from the evidence list: each evidence entry is a published alternate recipe, and its share is toGrams*toMassFactor / (fromGrams + toGrams*toMassFactor), assuming the replacement is mass-for-mass. min/median/max come from those shares; the shipped default is the minimum, so the claim is the conservative end of what real recipes do.
Only derived facts are stored (foods, grams, servings, links). No recipe text. Pages were read by hand on the 'checked' date; links can rot, so re-check before showing one.
Every changed food (from and to) must have an emission factor in data/food-map.json or the rule fails validation. Foods without carbon numbers are never swapped.

toMassFactor converts the listed replacement into the rule's 'to' state: dry lentils to cooked is about 2.4 (cooked lentils are roughly 2.3-2.6 times the dry weight; approximate), canned drained weights are already comparable (1).

rules.title: Blend some of the beef with lentils

evidence.source: Queensland Health, beef and lentil bolognese
evidence.note: 420 g can brown lentils, drained weight estimated at 60% of the can

evidence.source: Kitchen Confidante, beef and lentil chili
evidence.note: 1 cup dry French lentils; recipe also uses 4 oz pancetta

evidence.source: Yankee Magazine, lentil and beef chili

tips: Use cooked brown or green lentils, drained well and lightly mashed so they blend into the meat.
Brown the meat first, then fold in the lentils for the last few minutes.
Season a little more boldly: lentils are mild.
caveats: A little lower in protein per serving than all-beef, with more fibre.
Estimates use French production data (ADEME AGRIBALYSE); real values vary by farm and country.

dishCaveats.text: Texture is softer in burgers: chill the patties before cooking.
